classical_inputs.title: Finite cyclotomic, valuation, and local unit-root facts
classical_inputs.statement: Galois group and integral basis of Q(zeta_n), cyclotomic inertia and arithmetic Frobenius, tame inertia on roots of a uniformizer, and Hensel lifting of prime-to-residue-characteristic roots of units.
classical_inputs.reference: Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08, §§6–7; standard finite cyclotomic theory.

classical_inputs.title: Finite Chebotarev density
classical_inputs.statement: Every conjugacy class in a finite Galois extension of number fields has positive Dirichlet density; any fixed finite set of primes may be excluded.
classical_inputs.reference: Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08, Theorem8.31.

classical_inputs.title: Hilbert class field and Artin isomorphism
classical_inputs.statement: The Hilbert class field has Galois group the ideal class group under the Artin map; together with Chebotarev this gives degree-one primes in prescribed ideal classes outside finite exclusions.
classical_inputs.reference: Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03, V Theorem3.6, Corollary3.7, Example3.9.

classical_inputs.title: Kummer exact sequence and Hilbert90
classical_inputs.statement: H1(Q,mu_p)=Q^times/Q^{times p}, compatibly with local restriction, from the Kummer sequence and H1(Gal(L/K),L^times)=0.
classical_inputs.reference: Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03, II Proposition1.22, together with the Kummer exact sequence.

simplifications: An arbitrary fixed Bernoulli denominator-clearing integer replaces the source explicit Stk.dk in the asymptotic congruence; the final literal den(N,k) is retained.
The zero algebraic-value case is handled by v(0)=infinity, so the supplier does not need analytic Bernoulli nonvanishing.
Residual cyclotomic vanishing is proved by the finite Kummer group of Q and local valuation conditions.
Complex conjugation itself normalizes cocycles and establishes the required oddness, sufficient for the final source interface.
The finite subgroup-avoidance and length-induction arguments are written directly, retaining all simultaneous prime conditions.
